title: Weather, seasons, and small talk that always works
title_target: ອາກາດເປັນແນວໃດ — Aa-kàat pen neeo-dai
goal: Talk about the weather — the safest conversation opener in the world — name Laos's three seasons, and complain about the heat in a way that makes people laugh, not pity you.

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — On the office veranda, late May
dialogs.intro: The rainy season has just begun. Notice how Lao speakers guess at things without committing — a language habit that makes conversation feel gentler.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ມື້ນີ້|Mʉ̂ʉ-nîi][ຮ້ອນ|hâwn][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai][ເນາະ|nāw]
lines.id: It's so hot today, isn't it?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຮ້ອນ|Hâwn][ໂພດ|phôot] [ຢູ່|Yùu][ອິນໂດເນເຊຍ|in-doo-nee-sia][ກໍ|kaw][ຮ້ອນ|hâwn] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ຢູ່|yùu][ນີ້|nîi][ຮ້ອນ|hâwn][ກວ່າ|kwàa]
lines.id: Way too hot. It's hot in Indonesia too, but it's hotter here.
lines.literal: hot — too-much. at — Indonesia — also — hot. but — at — here — hot — more.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ເດືອນ|Dʉan][ຫ້າ|hāa][ຮ້ອນ|hâwn][ທີ່ສຸດ|thìi-sút] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ດຽວ|dǐao][ຝົນ|fǒn][ຊິ|si][ຕົກ|tók][ແລ້ວ|lèeo]
lines.id: May is the hottest. But the rain will start soon.
lines.literal: month — five — hot — most. but — soon — rain — will — fall — already.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຝົນ|Fǒn][ຕົກ|tók][ດົນ|dón][ບໍ່|bàw]

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຕົກ|Tók][ໜັກ|nak] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ບໍ່|bàw][ດົນ|dón] [ໜຶ່ງ|Nʉ̀ng][ຊົ່ວໂມງ|sùa-móong][ກໍ|kaw][ເຊົາ|sao] [ແລ້ວ|Lèeo][ກໍ|kaw][ເຢັນ|yén][ສະບາຍ|sa-baai]
lines.id: It pours, but not for long. It stops within an hour. Then it's nice and cool.
lines.literal: fall — heavy. but — not — long. one — hour — then — stop. after — then — cool — comfortable.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຕອນ|Tawn][ນີ້|nîi][ຟ້າ|fâa][ມືດ|mʉ̂ʉt][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ຄື|Khʉʉ][ຊິ|si][ຝົນ|fǒn][ຕົກ|tók]
lines.id: The sky's already dark. Looks like rain.
lines.literal: time — this — sky — dark — already. like — will — rain — fall.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ແມ່ນ|Mèen] [ເຈົ້າ|Jâo][ຄວນ|khuan][ເອົາ|ao][ຄັນ|khán][ຮົ່ມ|hòm][ໄປ|pai][ນຳ|nám]
lines.id: Yes. You should take an umbrella.
lines.literal: true. you — should — take — (classifier) — umbrella — go — along.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ບໍ່ມີ|bàw míi][ຮົ່ມ|hòm] [ຢືມ|Yʉʉm][ໄດ້|dâi][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: I don't have an umbrella. Can I borrow one?
lines.literal: I — not — have — umbrella. borrow — can — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi][ເລີຍ| lóei] [ຢູ່|Yùu][ໃນ|nai][ຫ້ອງ|hàwng][ພຸ້ນ|phûn] [ໜາວ|Nǎao][ບໍ່|bàw][ຕອນ|tawn][ກາງຄືນ|kaang-khʉ́ʉn]
lines.id: Sure. It's in the room over there. Do you find the nights cold?
lines.literal: can — right-away. be-at — in — room — over-there. cold — (question) — time — night?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່|Bàw][ໜາວ|nǎao] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ໝູ່|mùu][ຂ້ອຍ|khàwy][ວ່າ|vàa][ເດືອນ|dʉan][ສິບສອງ|síp-sǎwng][ໜາວ|nǎao][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ແມ່ນ|Mèen][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Not cold. But my friend says December is really cold. Is that right?
lines.literal: not — cold. but — friend — my — say — month — twelve — cold — much. true — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ແມ່ນ|Mèen] [ຢູ່|Yùu][ພາກ|phâak][ເໜືອ|nʉ̌a][ໜາວ|nǎao][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ຕ້ອງ|Tâwng][ໃສ່|sài][ເສື້ອ|sʉ̂a][ກັນ|kan][ໜາວ|nǎao]
lines.id: That's right. It's very cold in the north. You need a jacket.
lines.literal: true. at — region — north — cold — much. must — wear — shirt — guard — cold.

notes: **ອາກາດ aa-kàat = "weather" and also "air".** *ອາກາດເປັນແນວໃດ* (what's the weather like), *ອາກາດດີ* (nice weather), *ອາກາດບໍ່ດີ* (bad weather). It's a safe conversation opener anywhere, with anyone.

**ຝົນຕົກ fǒn tók = "it's raining", literally "rain falls".** The word *ຕົກ tók* is used for anything that comes down: *ຫິມະຕົກ* (it's snowing), *ຕົກລົງ* (fall down; also: agree). For the rain stopping, it's *ຝົນເຊົາ fǒn sao*.

**ຮ້ອນ hâwn = hot, ໜາວ nǎao = cold (weather and body), ເຢັນ yén = cool/cold (things).** ⚠️ The *ໜາວ* / *ເຢັນ* difference matters: *ຂ້ອຍໜາວ* (I'm cold), but *ນ້ຳເຢັນ* (cold water). Saying *ຂ້ອຍເຢັນ* sounds like "my body has a low temperature" — odd, though understood.
**ຄືຊິ khʉʉ si = "looks like it's going to…", and it's how Lao speakers guess.** *ຄືຊິຝົນຕົກ* (looks like rain). On its own, *ຄື khʉʉ* means "like, similar": *ຄືກັນ* (the same), *ຄືເຈົ້າ* (like you).
**ຄວນ khuan = "should", placed before the verb.** *ເຈົ້າຄວນເອົາຮົ່ມໄປ* (you should take an umbrella). It's softer than *ຕ້ອງ tâwng* (must), and far more common for making suggestions.
**ວ່າ vàa = "say that", and it introduces reported speech.** *ໝູ່ຂ້ອຍວ່າ…* (my friend says…), *ຂ້ອຍຄິດວ່າ…* (I think that…), *ເພິ່ນວ່າ…* (they say…). It's the key link word for starting a story.
**ດຽວ dǐao = "in a moment, soon".** *ດຽວຝົນຊິຕົກ* (it's going to rain soon). Doubled as *ດຽວໆ dǐao-dǐao*, it means "wait, wait" — used to stop someone.

**ເສື້ອກັນໜາວ sʉ̂a kan nǎao = "jacket", literally "cold-guard shirt".** The pattern *ກັນ kan* (guard against, prevent) appears in many objects: *ຄັນຮົ່ມກັນຝົນ* (rain umbrella), *ຢາກັນຍຸງ* (mosquito repellent).

**About "cold" in Laos.** In Vientiane, December–January drops to 15–18°C and locals really do wear thick jackets. In the northern highlands — Xiengkhouang, Phongsaly — mornings can get close to freezing. Don't go there in December with just a T-shirt.

grammars.title: Weather: words for every condition
after: Notice **ຟ້າ *fâa***, "sky", which attaches to many kinds of weather: *ຟ້າມືດ* (dark sky), *ຟ້າຮ້ອງ* (sky shouts = thunder), *ຟ້າຜ່າ* (sky splits = lightning), *ຟ້າແຈ້ງ* (clear sky).

grammars.title: Three seasons, not four
after: The word **ລະດູ *la-dùu*** means "season", and it can be dropped in conversation: just *ຕອນໜາວ* (in the cold time), *ຕອນຝົນ* (in the rainy time).

The rainy season in Laos rarely means rain all day. The pattern: clear morning, a heavy downpour for an hour or two in the afternoon, then a cool evening. It's actually the most beautiful season for waterfalls and rice fields — and the one with the fewest tourists.

blocks.text: **ຈົນ *jon*** means "so … that, until" and links cause and effect: *ຮ້ອນຈົນເຫື່ອອອກ* (so hot I'm sweating), *ແຊບຈົນລືມອີ່ມ* (so tasty you forget you're full). It's a link word that makes your sentences come alive.
⚠️ *ຮົ່ມ hòm* means "umbrella" **and** "shade". Its classifier is *ຄັນ khán*, the same as for vehicles — so one umbrella is *ຄັນຮົ່ມໜຶ່ງຄັນ*.

sections.title: Compass directions and the geography of Laos

blocks.text: Notice **ຕາເວັນ *taa-wén***, "sun" — literally "eye of the day". East is *ຕາເວັນອອກ* (sun comes out), west is *ຕາເວັນຕົກ* (sun falls). The same logic as English "sunrise" and "sunset".

Laos is the only country in Southeast Asia with **no sea**. That's why the Mekong River — *ແມ່ນ້ຳຂອງ mèe-nâm Khǒong* — is not just a river; it's a highway, a source of fish, a national border, and the place people sit every evening. If you want one place to understand Laos, sit on its bank as the sun goes down.
